desc: Offline design only. A reboot scrubs DRAM (evidence/2026-07-30-t6040-daily-driver-object-c1529d4c.md), so ramoops cannot hold a panic that ends in the watchdog reset. A kdump crash kernel loaded with kexec -p runs in place on panic, without iBoot, and can save pstore and /proc/vmcore. Tasks: check the 5019 .config for KEXEC_CORE, CRASH_DUMP, PROC_VMCORE, CRASH_RESERVE; size a crashkernel= reservation from the live map in evidence/2026-10-30-t6040-5026-live-facts-for-crash-kernel.md, not from the 5019 DTS comment's chainload addresses (live: kernel code 0x10008000000, FDT 0x1000de38000). There is no RAM below 4 GiB, so plain crashkernel=<size> (DMA32 first) will not work: use an explicit base in the second RAM block, clear of ramoops (0x10300000000 + 2 MiB) and the reserved blocks (candidate 512M@0x10500000000), or ,high, checked against /proc/iomem on the boot that carries it. Keep it out of the first block, where the 5015 CTRR_C window is. The crash kernel's own cmdline needs nr_cpus=1 (5024), so it never tries to start the parked spin-table secondaries; decide whether the crash kernel may write p3 at all (no Flush, 5006: it would need its own clean controller shutdown) or only keeps the record in RAM for a following kexec. arm64 machine_kexec_prepare skips the stuck-CPU refusal for KEXEC_TYPE_CRASH (seen in the Gravity tree; confirm in the 5019 tree), so kexec -p may load on a maxcpus=1 kernel without nr_cpus=1 (the 5024 object). Otherwise it uses the kexec path that 5021 tests. Deliverable: a kbuild flag proposal and a bounded rig ticket draft; nothing built or booted. LIVE FACTS 2026-10-30 (on-device session, evidence/2026-10-30-t6040-5026-live-facts-for-crash-kernel.md): config has KEXEC_CORE/CRASH_RESERVE/CRASH_DUMP/PROC_VMCORE/RELOCATABLE=y; no crashkernel= on this boot (kexec_crash_size 0); no RAM below 4 GiB, so plain crashkernel=<size> likely fails its low allocation; candidate crashkernel=512M@0x10500000000 or ,high; running Kernel code starts at 0x10008000000.
